Its second intersection with the circle gives the displayed parametrization; writing t=m/n in lowest terms gives the stated exclusions."},{"claim":"The reduced denominator is r², where r=q/gcd(q,2), and r is odd, at least 5, and has only prime divisors congruent to 1 modulo 4.","reasoning":"For odd p|q, primitiveness implies p divides neither m nor n; if p also divided n²−m², the congruences would force 2m²≡0 mod p, a contradiction. If q is even, m,n are odd, q≡2 mod 8 and 8|n²−m², so precisely a factor 4 cancels at 2. Each odd p|r makes −1 a quadratic residue modulo p, hence p≡1 mod 4. The excluded m=±n case and the minimum possible values of q give r≥5."},{"claim":"The reduced numerator is divisible by 24.","reasoning":"If q is odd, mn is even, so 8|N; if q is even, 8|n²−m² and the factor 4 cancellation leaves the reduced numerator divisible by 8. Modulo 3, either 3|mn or m² and n² are both 1 modulo 3, so 3|N. In the even-q case 3∤q; odd primes dividing q do not cancel with N.
